22 What are the SI base units of stress?
A
kg m s–2
B
kg m–1
s–2
C
kg m–2
s–2
D
kg m–3
s–2

hints: Start from what stress means in deformation of solids: stress is force divided by cross-sectional area.
Recall the SI base units of the newton from $F = ma$: $\text{kg}$ for mass times $\text{m s}^{-2}$ for acceleration.
Divide the force units by the unit of area, $\text{m}^{2}$, and combine the powers of $\text{m}$ to get the base units of stress.
walkthrough: Identify the defining equation: stress $= \frac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}$, so its unit is the newton divided by the square metre.
Write force in SI base units using $F = ma$: mass is $\text{kg}$ and acceleration is $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Write area in SI base units: $1 \text{ m}^{2}$.
Divide to get stress units: $\frac{\text{kg m s}^{-2}}{\text{m}^{2}} = \text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$.
Check against the options: only the option with $\text{kg}$ to power 1, $\text{m}$ to power -1 and $\text{s}$ to power -2 matches. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is the base-unit form of force, the newton, $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$. Stress divides force by area so one more power of $\text{m}$ must be removed.

B.explanation: Force $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ divided by area $\text{m}^{2}$ gives $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$, which is the unit of stress and pressure.

C.explanation: This has one extra $\text{m}^{-1}$. It would correspond to force divided by volume, not force divided by area.

D.explanation: This is force divided by volume, with units $\text{kg m}^{-3}\text{s}^{-2}$. Stress uses area $\text{m}^{2}$, not volume $\text{m}^{3}$.
